name: Sonnet+tools small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Long-only basket of small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech growth names sized by current momentum and stress-window resilience, with a cash buffer

positions.thesis: Samsara pulled back to $39.79 (-3.3% on 8/14, likely broad-market not company-specific) but Strong Buy consensus and the $44.31 avg PT (~11% upside) are unchanged; no negative catalyst, held at prior sizing as the highest-conviction leader.

Rubrik ripped 13.5% this week to $102.23 on the Wipro AI-resilience launch, and for the first time is trading ABOVE the $96.07 consensus PT (-6% implied) -- the same pattern that justified cutting S and PATH last week. Strong Buy rating and product momentum are still intact and Aug 27 earnings are a real catalyst, so trimmed rather than closed, locking in gains and reducing size into event risk with reward/risk now compressed.

Affirm at $78.35 has lagged well behind last week's aggressive PT hikes (BofA $93, Goldman $106, Citi $115 -- 19-47% implied upside), the largest gap-to-target in the book; upsized into the Aug 27 print as the best remaining risk/reward.

Flywire announced a Trustly open-banking partnership expansion (8/12) and drew fresh PT hikes to $22-24 (Morgan Stanley, B.Riley, Goldman) above the $20.54 consensus; stock up 3.1% to $18.81 on 8/14 while broader momentum names sold off. Upsized on continuing momentum despite the Q2 EPS miss.
Toast's Q2 beat/raise thesis is unchanged; $42-45 analyst PTs still imply ~25-30% upside from the $34.75 close. Held flat, no new information to act on.

SoFi trading mid-range ($18.29, within the $16-19 band Cramer flagged) with post-earnings analyst cuts (Goldman $18, MS $15) still capping upside despite record loan growth. Held at the already-reduced size with a tight stop.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Weekly reassessment through 8/14 close: two names (S, PATH) that were already flagged last week as having lost their price-target edge extended further above consensus targets with fresh insider-selling headlines, confirming the 'no edge left' thesis to the point of closing rather than just trimming.
